1yr •
🚀 Diving Deep into Hotel Booking Data with SQL!
Just wrapped up an exciting project where I explored hotel booking data to uncover customer behaviors, occupancy trends, and booking patterns across India. 📊
💡 Key Insights:
✔️ Found the top 5 customers who book the most in their home cities
✔️ Analyzed how much revenue and bookings come from female customers
✔️ Identified customers who book hotels in different states
✔️ Calculated how full each hotel gets each month to understand their performance
Big thanks to Ankit Bansal for providing this project in the bootcamp – it’s been a fantastic learning experience and a great opportunity to sharpen my SQL skills. 🙏
💬 Open to any suggestions or improvements on the SQL queries – always looking to learn and grow!
Stay tuned for Part 2, where I’ll be diving even deeper into customer segmentation and advanced analytics. Can’t wait to share more!
#SQL #DataAnalysis #HotelIndustry #CareerGrowth #LearningJourney #BootcampProject

ai_analysis.summary: This is a brief personal-project announcement about analyzing hotel booking data across India with SQL. The project reportedly examined customer booking behavior, identified the top five customers by bookings in their home cities, analyzed revenue and booking volume from female customers, identified customers who booked in different states, and assessed monthly hotel occupancy as a performance indicator. It does not include SQL queries, results, figures, dataset details, or a Power BI implementation. Customer segmentation and advanced analytics are mentioned only as planned topics for a future second part.
subtopics: Top customers by bookings in home cities
Revenue and booking volume from female customers
concepts: Revenue and Booking Volume by Customer Gender

interview_questions.question: In a portfolio interview, how would you summarize the analytical scope of the hotel booking project?
interview_questions.answer:
The project examined customer behavior, occupancy trends, and booking patterns in hotel data from India.
It identified the top five customers by booking frequency in their home cities.
It analyzed revenue and booking volume contributed by female customers.
It identified customers who booked hotels in different states.
It evaluated how full each hotel was each month as an indicator of performance.
